title: Immobilization of lipid nanorods onto two-dimensional crystals of protein tamavidin 2 for high-speed atomic force microscopy
protocol: Transform competent E. coli cells with the expression vector.
Grow the E. coli cells in LB medium containing an appropriate antibiotic until absorbance at 600 nm reaches 0.5–0.8.
Add IPTG to the LB medium and shake at ∼120 rpm for ∼18 h at 25°C.
Harvest the cells by centrifugation at 4°C (4000 × g for 10 min).
Store the cell pellet at −80°C.
Resuspend the pellet in Buffer L (50 mL) and add PMSF.
Sonicate the suspension on ice using ∼200 W power for 10 min with a pulse of 0.2 s followed by an interval of 0.8 s.
Centrifuge the suspension at 4°C (18,000 × g for 40 min) and collect the supernatant.
Purify the clear supernatant using 2-iminobiotin agarose.
Transfer 2-iminobiotin agarose resin slurry into an empty column.
Equilibrate the column with Buffer L.
Apply the supernatant to the column.
Wash the column with Buffer W.
Elute tamavidin 2 protein by adding Buffer E.
Concentrate the eluted tamavidin 2 solution using Amicon Ultra-15.
Exchange buffer to Buffer S during concentration.
Centrifuge the tamavidin 2 solution at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Collect the supernatant after centrifugation.
Concentrate the tamavidin 2 solution up to 150 μM.
Prepare a lipid mixture containing galactosylceramide, biotinyl cap PE, POPC, POPE, PI, POPS, POPA, and cardiolipin in chloroform.
Dry the lipid mixture under a gentle stream of nitrogen gas to form a lipid film.
Place the glass bottle with the lipid film in a vacuum desiccator for at least 2 hours to completely evaporate the chloroform.
Add 100 μL of buffer (e.g., 20 mM HEPES-NaOH containing 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.0) to the lipid film.
Incubate the mixture for 10 minutes followed by vortexing to prepare a 1 mM lipid solution.
Transfer the lipid solution to a 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tube.
Sonicate the lipid solution in a bath sonicator for 10 minutes at 40 W and 42 kHz.
Further sonicate with a tip sonicator for no more than 5 seconds at 50 W and 20 kHz.
Protect from light and keep the microcentrifuge tube on ice until use.
Prepare crystal buffer and fixation buffer.
Add 1 μL of 150 μM tamavidin 2 to 20 μL of crystal buffer.
Mix gently by pipetting.
Incubate the mixture for 5 min after dilution with crystal buffer.
Deposit a drop (∼2 μL) of the diluted tamavidin 2 solution onto freshly cleaved mica using scotch tape.
Incubate the deposited solution on mica for 5 min.
Rinse the mica surface with 0.01% glutaraldehyde diluted with fixation buffer.
Keep the last drop on the mica for 5 minutes.
Rinse the mica surface with imaging buffer before HS-AFM imaging.
Set up HS-AFM and start imaging.
Confirm 2D crystals of tamavidin 2 formed on the mica surface.
Keep a drop of imaging buffer on the mica after HS-AFM imaging.
Fix a sheet of Kimwipes with scotch tape in a plastic Petri dish and wet it with Milli-Q water to create humidity.
Place a drop of buffer solution (∼2 μL) on mica.
Loosely fix the glass stage to the bottom of the Petri dish with double-sided adhesive tape.
Seal the space between the container and lid with parafilm.
Mix 9 μl of buffer solution (e.g., 20 mM HEPES-NaOH containing 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.0) and 1 μL of lipid solution to prepare a 0.1 mM lipid solution.
Exchange the buffer solution on tamavidin 2 2D crystals for the prepared 0.1 mM lipid solution.
Keep a drop of 0.1 mM lipid solution on mica for 5 minutes.
Set up HS-AFM and start imaging.
Apply proteins of interest to lipid nanorods immobilized on tamavidin 2 2D crystals after removing the glass stage from the HS-AFM setup.
Add proteins of interest to the imaging buffer while performing HS-AFM imaging.
Incubate proteins with lipid nanorods before applying them to tamavidin 2 2D crystals if necessary.
